title: Artificial Komal Notes
summary: Pathak ji's fix for komal Re and Dha, which are hard to get by half-lifting a finger: narrow those holes with a plug, such as a rosary bead whose small hole is widened while testing on Bhairav or Toḍī, or with a piece of pipe that turns over the holes or slides inside the tube.

blocks.verse:
रिध कोमल रागेषु सौविध्याय सुरैषिणाम्।
कृत्रिमौ कोमलौ कार्यौ वाद्ये रिषभधैवतौ।55।
blocks.text: For the convenience of those who seek tunefulness, in rāgas with komal Re and Dha, an artificial komal Ṛṣabha and Dhaivata should be made on the instrument.

After the 12 notes in all have been placed in the bānsurī by the rules above, a bānsurī can be made and played, on the basis of those svarasthāna (note positions), with at least six and at most 10 holes. Even so, the problem of lifting half a finger for komal Ṛṣabha and Dhaivata could not be solved. So by a scientific method I made komal Re and Dha, and they also worked in playing. For this the holes of Re and Dha must be made smaller in some way. That device can be of any material: rubber, wood and so on.

blocks.verse:
माला खण्डेन वाऽन्र्येन काष्ठोपकरणेन च।
पूरणीयौ ऋधौ तत्र लघु छिद्रं यथा भवेत्।56।
blocks.text: Re and Dha should there be filled with a piece of a bead-string, or with some other wooden device, so that a small hole results.

This solution is possible in 3 ways. 1 Take one bead out of some mālā (string of beads) and seat it on the hole like a guṭakā (plug), so that the hole is closed like a phial [with its stopper]. Then the small hole of that plug should be enlarged only so far that the komal note is heard exactly right. But this procedure will not succeed in a six-hole bānsurī, because in it Re, on becoming komal, will spoil the Gāndhāra lying next to it. Although this difficulty occurs in the nine-hole bānsurī too, in it a light chhallā (ring) is put into the separately made holes of komal Ga and Ni, and when Re and Dha are made komal those rings are removed. Or else bend a brass strip and put it inside the pipe, so that inside it fits to the very shape of the pipe, and by sliding it komal Gāndhāra can be brought back to how it was.

blocks.verse:
अर्धमानात् तृतीयांशः परिमाण स्तयोर्भवेत्।
पूरकस्थूलता म्पश्यन् रागं पश्यन् मुहुर्मुहुः।57।
blocks.text: Their size should be from half to a third of the [original] measure, watching the thickness of the plug and watching the rāga again and again.

That is, in the pūraka (plug, guṭakā) by which a hole is closed, a hole smaller than that hole, from half down to a quarter of it, should be made in that plug, and the hole should be enlarged according to the thickness of that plug. And while enlarging, enlarge it little by little, and keep testing its komal quality by playing rāga Bhairav or Toḍī again and again.

The second method of making this artificial Ṛṣabha is as follows. Shave that much of the pipe with something and make it smooth. Close the place, the part in which the Re and Ga holes lie, with a piece of some other pipe. Then, according to rāga Toḍī, make a small hole for Re and a large hole for komal Ga [in it]. Now, when that piece is turned, the holes beneath will be closed; then, in it, facing the holes of the original pipe beneath, let two holes be made according to śuddha Re and Ga. The four holes of that upper pipe, skilfully made, will turn by turns over the two holes beneath, and komal or śuddha notes will be formed as you wish. But some rāgas with both Ṛṣabhas will get no benefit from this artificial note. So for those rāgas one will have to adopt the mūrchanā paddhati (method of shifting Sa), changing Sa. The third method is this: instead of putting a pipe over the pipe, if some thin piece of the same size is fitted inside the pipe, then by sliding the inner pipe one way the Re hole will become small and the Ga hole large, and by sliding it upward the Ga hole will become small and the Re hole large. But in this procedure air passes through because of the looseness, so the procedure does not succeed as well. Like Re and Dha, Ga and Ni too can be made artificial.
